title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 75-77, 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes', section B.1). Start with an object (X,C) of the complex-analytic Teichmüller groupoid with boundary. X is a compact Riemann surface with boundary, assumed connected, of type (g,ν). C is a system of disjoint simple closed curves, and Grothendieck imposes a 'differential condition', meaning some smooth collar or tangent data along C and ∂X.

Step 1 (previous page). Cut X along C to get X'. Cap every hole canonically with a holomorphic disk, using the tangent data along ∂X'. The result is a compact Riemann surface without boundary, X''. It carries a family of pointed holomorphic disks. These disks are paired by antiholomorphic isomorphisms (each pair comes from the two sides of one curve of C), except for the ν disks that cap the original boundary ∂X.

Step 2 (this page). Build a nodal curve X'''. For each pair of disks, identify their two centres to form a node. Mark the centres of the remaining ν disks as punctures. X'' is then the normalization of a Deligne-Mumford stable curve X''' of type (g,ν), at least when C is admissible, e.g. a pants-type system with no disk or annulus components.

Step 3 (this page). Each node x has preimages {x1,x2} in X''. The antiholomorphic isomorphism between the two pointed disks yields a well-defined nonzero element of T_{x1}X'' ⊗_C T_{x2}X''. Concretely:
- Let z1 and z2 be centred coordinates mapping the disks onto the unit disk; each is unique up to a rotation.
- An antiholomorphic map fixing the centres has the form z2 = c·conj(z1) with |c|=1.
- On the unit circle this agrees with the holomorphic gluing z1·z2 = c.
- So the pair (z1,z2) is canonical up to the diagonal action, and the anti-isomorphism gives the nonzero vector c·∂/∂z1 ⊗ ∂/∂z2.
Grothendieck restates this as an element of T*_{x1} ∧^{C*} T*_{x2}. Here T* most likely means the punctured tangent line, a C*-torsor, and ∧^{C*} is the contracted product of torsors; the result is canonically (T1⊗T2)∖{0}. This is precisely the node-smoothing ('plumbing') parameter in the standard local model z1 z2 = t.

Conclusion. There is a functor between two groupoids:
- (a) source: compact holomorphic curves with boundary of type (g,ν), with the disk/collar data;
- (b) target: complex algebraic stable curves of type (g,ν) equipped with (1) a 'structure de propagateurs' at the singular points (a nonzero element of T1⊗T2 at each node) and (2) an admissible system of disks around the marked points.
The next page passes to moduli stacks ('multiplicités modulaires'): a morphism MDB_{g,ν} → MND^{st}_{g,ν}. It is compatible with the maps to the category of combinatorial types, namely Mumford-Deligne dual graphs with weighted vertices and oriented torus data on the edges.

Purpose. Describe the 'surgery' (cutting and plumbing) of conformal surfaces algebro-geometrically. The aim is to embed the analytic Teichmüller groupoid with boundary into structures living over the boundary of the Deligne-Mumford compactification, as part of the Teichmüller tower programme of the Esquisse.
errors: The modulus of the element of T1⊗T2 is not independent data. Once the disks are fixed (with intrinsic unit radius), only the phase c is new; the size is already determined by the disk system. So the 'propagator' structure overlaps with the disk data, and the functor is presumably far from an equivalence unless the target remembers the disks at the nodes too. The text does not address this.
Stability of X''' needs an admissibility condition on C: no curve bounding a disk or a once-punctured disk, and no two curves cobounding an annulus. This is implicit, not stated.

The direction 'antiholomorphic isomorphism of pointed disks ⇒ element of T1⊗T2' relies on the observation that an anti-isomorphism z ↦ c·conj(z) corresponds to the holomorphic gluing z1 z2 = c on the circle. This is correct but left implicit.

'i.e. [deux] élément' should read 'i.e. un élément'. The T* notation must mean punctured tangent spaces (C*-torsors), not cotangent spaces; otherwise the equality with nonzero elements of T⊗T is off by a dualization, which is harmless but notationally inconsistent.

ideas.what: Cut a Riemann surface along a curve system, cap the holes with canonical disks, and identify paired disk centres to get a stable nodal curve whose normalization is the capped surface.
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing / degeneration to the Deligne-Mumford boundary along a pants-type decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fay (1973), Earle-Marden, Masur (1976), Bers, Kra; Wolpert for plumbing coordinates
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower, surgery and 'multiplicités modulaires' in general terms; this explicit construction is not there as far as I know.

ideas.what: The anti-isomorphism of the two pointed disks at a node gives a nonzero element of T_{x1}⊗T_{x2}, written as a contracted product of C*-torsors of punctured tangent lines. Grothendieck calls it a 'structure de propagateurs'.
ideas.modern_name: Node-smoothing parameter / tangent-tensor (log-structure) data at nodes; phase version = 'decorated' or real-oriented blow-up of the DM boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deformation theory of nodes (Deligne-Mumford 1969); log structures on nodal curves (F. Kato, Kato-Nakayama 1990s); phase-decorated boundary (Kimura-Stasheff-Voronov 1995); 'propagators' as plumbing collars in closed string field theory (Zwiebach ~1990)

ideas.what: A functor from the groupoid of bordered holomorphic surfaces with disk/collar data to the groupoid of stable curves with propagator structure and admissible marked disks. It induces a morphism of moduli stacks MDB_{g,ν} → MND^{st}_{g,ν}, compatible with the maps to combinatorial types (dual graphs with torus data on edges).
ideas.modern_name: Comparison map from moduli of bordered/framed Riemann surfaces to a decorated (log or real-blown-up) Deligne-Mumford compactification, stratified by dual graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (CFT, 1987-88), Kimura-Stasheff-Voronov (1995), Costello (2000s), Looijenga's work on Teichmüller towers
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse alludes to modular multiplicities and Mumford-Deligne stratifications; this functor itself is unpublished.

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck attaches to each node of a stable curve a nonzero tensor in T_{x1}⊗T_{x2} coming from gluing data of disks, calls it a 'propagator' structure, and organizes moduli by dual graphs with tori on edges. This is essentially the plumbing/propagator formalism of later conformal and string field theory (Segal 1987, Zwiebach's closed SFT ~1990, Kimura-Stasheff-Voronov 1995). It also matches log structures on nodal curves (Kato) and the tangential-basepoint data used in Ihara-Nakamura's arithmetic Teichmüller theory.
missed.quote: un élément non nul (i.e. une base) de T_{X'',x1} ⊗_C T_{X'',x2} ... munies 1°) d'une "structure de propagateurs" en ses pts singuliers
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, independent formulation of the decorated DM boundary (log or framed nodes) motivated by Teichmüller groupoids. It could be credited in histories of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller programme and linked to the KSV/Costello operadic picture.

missed.claim: The comparison morphism MDB_{g,ν} → MND^{st}_{g,ν} of moduli stacks, compatible with combinatorial types, is announced ('on trouve sûrement un morphisme') but not proved. Its properties (fibres, whether it is a homotopy equivalence onto a real-blown-up boundary neighbourhood) are left open.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi une fonction[foncteur] de a) catégorie des courbes hol. cptes à bord ... vers b) Catégorie des courbes C-alg. stables
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise question about the relation between bordered moduli (TCFT/Segal side) and log-DM moduli (arithmetic side). It is partly addressed in later literature but not in this Teichmüller-tower framing.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical plumbing. The notable points are that it is phrased as a functor of groupoids into stable curves decorated with C*-torsor data at nodes, and that the term 'propagateurs' anticipates string field theory and log-structure formalisms. Interesting historically, but not a hidden theorem.

'On trouve ainsi une fonction de' → probably 'un foncteur de'
'courbes hol. cptes i.bord' → 'courbes hol. cptes à bord'
'structure de propagation [?] / "ensemble"' → likely '"structure de propagateurs"' (consistent with the next page: 'structure de propagateurs (N)')
